newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end up on optimism, bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end up on optimism, bargain-hunting.

text.p: Brazil stocks ended higher as investors picked up cheap shares amid continued optimism on Cia Vale do Rio Doce's privatization and reports the government will not impose new credit restrictions, brokers said.
"The market was in a buying mood but we may see some profit-taking tomorrow because it closed a little weak," a local trader told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares closed up 0.78 percent at 9,709 points on healthy trade of 648.3 million reais ($612 million).
Brokers said the bolsa continued Wednesday's technical rally as investors snapped up bargain shares, whose prices had been held down in the run-up to this week's options settlements.

Investor optimism remained strong through the day as most investors are upbeat about the prospects for state mining firm CVRD's selloff despite legal challenges and political opposition to next week's scheduled auction.
"As far as the market is concerned, if the sale is on, everything is beautiful," a trader at a local bank said.
Buying slowed at the end of the session, prompting speculation Friday's session will open on the decline, brokers said.
As usual, most of the trade was focused on bellwether Telebras, whose preferred share ended up 0.59 percent at 119.70 reais. Its common voter rose 0.8 percent to 114.40 reais.
CVRD's preferred share extended its 3.7 percent gain Wednesday by rising 1.12 percent in the session to close at 27.00 reais. Its common share, however, droped 1.34 percent to end at 29.50 reais.

Brazilian power stocks accompanied the rise, albeit at a slower pace. The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index rose 0.44 percent to end at 2,677 points, led by a 1.23 percent rise in Eletrobras' preferred to 495.00 reais.
